item.title: China-Indonesia "Sharp Knife 2026" army counter-terrorism joint training concludes
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
Chinese participating troops line up at the closing ceremony. (Photo by Xie Jiangshan) GUANGZHOU, Nov. 3 -- The China-Indonesia "Sharp Knife 2026" army counter-terrorism joint training concluded in Guangzhou on November 2. At the closing ceremony, commanders from both sides delivered remarks and awarded certificates to outstanding participating personnel. During the live-force phase, the participating troops conducted joint mountain counter-terrorism rescue operation, completing subjects including covert infiltration, coordinated rescue, and search and clearance. Since the training started on October 27, participating troops from both sides were organized into mixed formations to undergo specialized training, tactical coordination, and comprehensive exercises. The two sides also conducted thematic seminars, weapon and equipment displays, sports competitions, and cultural exchanges. As the third edition of this series of joint training, the Sharp Knife 2026 is of great significance for enhancing traditional friendship between the two countries, promoting bilateral defense cooperation, and safeguarding regional peace and stability.

item.title: Senior Chinese military official meets Russian defense minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- Senior Chinese military official Zhang Shengmin on Tuesday met with visiting Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov in Beijing. Zhang, vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, said China is ready to work with Russia to continuously strengthen strategic communication, better safeguard the two countries' respective sovereignty, security and development interests, and effectively safeguard world and regional peace and stability. Belousov said that Russia is ready to continue close coordination with China, strengthen strategic consultations, firmly support each other, expand practical cooperation in various fields, and push for more outcomes in the development of relations between the two countries and the two militaries.

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon. item.title: The Philippines Abuses Chairmanship to Put up Obstacles to China's Participation in ADMM-Plus: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct.29 -- "The Philippine side's willful acts to hijack ASEAN and stir up troubles would only undermine the credibility of ADMM-Plus, erode solidarity and mutual trust among ASEAN countries, and ultimately, impair the fundamental interests of the countries and peoples in the region, including the Philippines," said Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, spokesperson for China's defense ministry, at a regular press conference on Thursday. The spokesperson made the remarks while responding to media question about the absence of China's defense minister from this year's ADMM-Plus meeting in the Philippines. The spokesperson first confirmed that the ADMM-Plus is the highest-level and largest defense and security dialogue and cooperation mechanism in the Asia-Pacific. Established in 2010, it has served as an important platform for countries to build trust, strengthen cooperation, and uphold regional peace and stability. He then pointed out that as the rotating chair of this year's ADMM-Plus, the Philippine side has allowed a certain self-serving politician to act recklessly and abuse its chairmanship to put up obstacles to China's participation. The spokesperson seriously criticized such moves of the Philippine side, stating that they seriously violate ASEAN's principle of consensus through consultation and run counter to the open and inclusive spirit of the ADMM-Plus. "They do not conform to basic diplomatic protocols, and undermine China's legitimate rights as a member of the mechanism. Many ASEAN countries have raised questions and opposition over this," said the spokesperson. "Against such a backdrop, the Chinese side still decided to send representatives to attend the meeting, which demonstrates China's firm support to ASEAN centrality and responsible attitude towards regional defense and security cooperation," added the spokesperson.

item.title: Int’l community should stay on high alert against tricks played by Japan's right-wing forces: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct. 29 -- "Anyone familiar with history knows that manipulating public opinion first, fabricating excuses next and taking actions in the end is an old trick of Japanese militarists to launch aggression in the past," said Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on October 29, 2026. According to media reports, China’s PLANS Liaoning Carrier Task Group recently conducted far-seas training in the Western Pacific. The Japanese Self-Defense Force vessels and aircraft tracked and monitored the Chinese carrier task group, while some Japanese defense officials claimed that Japan's monitoring capabilities are limited and Japan needs to further strengthen its "defense posture". In response to the above reports, the spokesperson pointed out that the training of the PLANS Liaoning Carrier Task Group (CTG Liaoning) in relevant waters of the Western Pacific is a routine arrangement within the annual plan of the Chinese military. It aims to test and improve the combat capabilities of the CTG in the far seas, does not target any specific country or objective, and is in compliance with international law and international practices. "Many netizens refer to the Japanese side as a 'chief photographer' of the Chinese PLA Navy. These 'chief photographers' often spy on China's normal training and exercises, exaggerate the situation, deceive the Japanese public, mislead international public opinion, and make up excuses for Japan’s military expansion and reinforcement," added the spokesperson. "The international community should stay on high alert against such tricks played by Japan's right-wing forces, and resolutely curb the reckless moves of Japan's neo-militarism," stressed the spokesperson.
